newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian court rules out DNA test for president.
newsitem.headline: Zambian court rules out DNA test for president.

text.p: The Zambian Supreme Court on Wednesday threw out an application by opposition parties that President Frederick Chiluba undergo a DNA test to establish his parentage.
Opposition leaders challenging Chiluba's presidency say he lied about his parentage and nationality in his electoral nomination papers ahead of last year's November elections.
Under constitutional reforms last year, presidential candidates must be first-generation Zambians whose parents are also Zambian.
The opposition petition hinges on the testimony of Chabala Kafupi, who says he is Chiluba's biological father.
Kafupi told the court earlier this year he was originally from Zaire and that Chiluba was born in that country.
But Chief Justice Matthew Ngulube said Zambian law did not empower the court to force people to undergo DNA genetic tests.

The reforms requiring presidential candidates to be first-generation Zambians are widely seen to have been targeted at former President Kenneth Kaunda, who returned to active politics last year after he retired in 1992.
Kaunda's United National Independence Party and six other parties boycotted the elections after the reforms were passed.
